T: One plate. One strand. One meatball.
D: A pampered cocker spaniel falls for a streetwise stray who shows her life outside the yard.
P: Serve the mains when Tony brings out the spaghetti at the back of the restaurant.
S: Jim Dear's doughnuts with coffee caramel
Jim Dear dunking a doughnut at breakfast

Hot cinnamon sugar doughnuts made for dunking, with a silky coffee caramel dip, the breakfast Lady sits begging beside. Mix 400g plain flour, 7g dried yeast, 50g sugar, 1 egg, 40g soft butter and 200ml warm milk into a dough, knead 8 minutes and prove 1 hour. Roll 1cm thick, cut 12 rings and prove 20 minutes. Fry at 175C for 1 minute a side and toss in 100g sugar with 2 tsp cinnamon. For the dip, melt 150g brown sugar with 50g butter, add 150ml cream and 1 tsp instant coffee and simmer 3 minutes.
Italian bread split and spread with butter mashed with garlic, parsley and parmesan, baked at 200C for 12 minutes until crisp at the edges.
the candlelit table set for Lady and Tramp
Salami and provolone folded on a board with olives, marinated artichoke and roasted capsicum, with torn bread.
M: the famous spaghetti dinner behind Tony's
Beef and pork meatballs with parmesan and parsley, browned and simmered 40 minutes in a slow tomato and basil sauce, served over one big plate of spaghetti.
Tramp's back door chicken with salsa verde
Tramp doing his rounds of the back doors for scraps

Lemon, garlic and oregano chicken thighs roasted crisp-skinned, with smashed potatoes and a sharp caper salsa verde, the pick of the back-door rounds. Toss 1kg bone-in chicken thighs with the zest and juice of 1 lemon, 4 crushed garlic cloves, 2 tsp dried oregano, olive oil and salt. Roast skin up at 200C for 40 minutes until crisp. Boil 1kg baby potatoes 15 minutes, smash flat and roast alongside in oil for 30 minutes. Chop a bunch of parsley, a handful of basil, 1 tbsp capers and 1 garlic clove, and mix with lemon juice and 80ml olive oil. Spoon over the chicken.
W: Cannoli shells piped with ricotta whipped with icing sugar, orange zest and dark chocolate chips, the ends dipped in crushed pistachios.
K: Tony and Joe serenading the dinner out the back of Tony's

Blood orange juice and rosemary syrup topped with fizzing soda over ice, red as the checked tablecloth on Tony's back-step table. Simmer 80g caster sugar, 80ml water and 2 rosemary sprigs for 3 minutes, then cool and strain. In a jug, mix 500ml blood orange juice with the rosemary syrup and the juice of 1 lemon. Fill 4 glasses with ice, pour in the juice to halfway and top with soda water. Garnish each with a blood orange slice and a small rosemary sprig.

s.how: Mash 100g butter with crushed garlic, chopped parsley and grated parmesan. Split a loaf of Italian bread, spread thickly and bake at 200C for 12 minutes until crisp at the edges. Cut into thick slices and serve in the alley behind the restaurant.

s.note: the candlelit table set for Lady and Tramp
s.how: Fold 150g salami and slices of provolone onto a board. Add kalamata olives, marinated artichoke hearts and strips of roasted red capsicum. Tear a loaf of Italian bread beside it. Set it out for two by candlelight.

m.note: the famous spaghetti dinner behind Tony's
m.how: Mix 300g beef mince and 300g pork mince with parmesan, parsley and an egg, roll into balls and brown. Add 2 cans crushed tomatoes and torn basil and simmer 40 minutes. Pile over 500g spaghetti on one big plate. Leave the last meatball for your date.

w.how: Drain 500g ricotta overnight, then beat with 80g icing sugar, orange zest and 50g dark chocolate chips. Spoon into a piping bag and fill 12 cannoli shells just before serving. Dip each end in crushed pistachios.

d.note: Tony and Joe serenading the dinner out the back of Tony's
d.how: Simmer 80g caster sugar, 80ml water and 2 rosemary sprigs for 3 minutes, then cool and strain. In a jug, mix 500ml blood orange juice with the rosemary syrup and the juice of 1 lemon.
